s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of involuntary movements in an elderly patient with a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
salient_findings: Involuntary movements of the left upper and lower limbs
Slow response and reduced muscle strength in the left limbs
Positive tendon reflexes in the left limbs
High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI
key_facts: The patient is an 80-year-old woman
She has a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
She presented with involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs for more than 10 days
She had a slow response on neurological examination
She had reduced muscle strength in her left limbs
She had positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Her blood glucose level was 8.59 mmol/L
Her hemoglobin A1c was 7.43%
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
Brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Hemiballismus
shortlist.why_kept: Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude in the left arm and leg

shortlist.label: Diabetic striatal disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus and high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Vascular hemichorea
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of involuntary movements and slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions on noncontrast CT of the head

shortlist.label: Fahr's disease
shortlist.why_kept: High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia and basal ganglia calcification

shortlist.label: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation
shortlist.why_kept: High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia and slow response on neurological examination

raw.rationale: The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, combined with the presence of high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI and slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions on noncontrast CT of the head, are consistent with diabetic striatal disease, which is a rare condition associated with poorly controlled diabetes.

rejected.label: Hemiballismus
rejected.why: Hemiballismus is characterized by involuntary, violent, and large-amplitude movements, which does not exactly match the patient's presentation of continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude.

rejected.label: Vascular hemichorea
rejected.why: Vascular hemichorea is typically associated with a history of stroke or vascular disease, which is not mentioned in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Fahr's disease
rejected.why: Fahr's disease is a rare genetic disorder characterized by abnormal calcification of the basal ganglia, which is not suggested by the patient's MRI or CT findings.

rejected.label: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation
rejected.why: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation is a group of rare genetic disorders characterized by iron accumulation in the brain, which is not indicated by the patient's imaging studies.
